correctness.rationale: The finite domain is exhaustively traversed: connected graph masks, all nonedges, and all binary innate masks for n=2..5. Exact Fraction Gauss–Jordan with checked matrix inverses gives order-2..5 test counts 0,24,1344,100480 and strict increase counts 0,0,0,480. Orbit canonicalization under all 120 label permutations and the global sign flip yields exactly (58,0,9) and (185,1,11), 240 each. The analytical mean identity validates centered polarization comparisons; rank-one formula proves the five-path t>0 identity. All package paths point to the embedded verifier.

originality.rationale: Rácz–Rigobon (arXiv:2206.08996) already prove nonmonotonicity and the general edge-update identity with nonbinary opinions, but not the sharp five-vertex ±1 cutoff or the full 480-case two-orbit census. Other checked sources address either combined P+D or network optimizations rather than this exact binary finite boundary. Search failure alone is not novelty proof; residual unindexed-literature risk acknowledged.

value.rationale: The binary initial-opinion domain models dichotomous positions and is qualitatively more constrained than published three-agent real-opinion examples. The exact sharp minimum of five, complete 480-instance first-obstruction census, and two topological orbit types (path and triangle-tail) are a motivated finite mathematical classification, with an analytically persistent all-positive-weight path witness. No unproved large-n claim is needed.
